meaning:
δυνατός, -ή, -όν
(δύναμαι), [in LXX for גִּבּוֹר, חַיִל, etc. ;]
1. strong, mighty, powerful: absol., Luk.1:49, 1 Col.1:26; οἱ δ., the chief men, Act.25:5 ; of spiritual strength, Rom.15:1, 2Co.12:10 13:9; before ἐν, Luk.24:19, Act.7:22 18:24; πρός, 2Co.10:4.
2. C. inf., able to do; Luk.14:31, Act.11:17, Rom.4:21 11:23, 2Ti.1:12, Tit.1:9, Heb.11:19, Jas.3:2.
3. Neut., δυνατόν, possible: Mat.19:26, Mrk.9:23 10:27 14:36, Luk.18:27, Act.2:24 20:16; εἰ δ. (ἐστι), Mat.24:24 26:30, Mrk.13:22 14:35, Rom.12:18, Gal.4:15; τὸ δ. (= ἡ δύναμις) αὐτοῦ, Rom.9:22.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: Looking at them, Jesus said, “With men this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.”
Jesus said to him, “If you can believe, all things are possible to him who believes.”
For he who is mighty has done great things for me. Holy is his name.
whom God raised up, having freed him from the agony of death, because it was not possible that he should be held by it.
and being fully assured that what he had promised, he was also able to perform.
For you see your calling, brothers, that not many are wise according to the flesh, not many mighty, and not many noble;
for the weapons of our warfare are not of the flesh, but mighty before God to the throwing down of strongholds,
What was the blessing you enjoyed? For I testify to you that, if possible, you would have plucked out your eyes and given them to me.
